text:
Unionized workers at Seoul Metro launched a "work-to-rule" campaign Friday as they remain locked in a dispute with management over hiring and wages.
Under the collective action that began at 6 a.m., participants will fully adhere to safety regulations, such as maintaining train speeds regardless of subway schedules, in a move expected to slow down operations.
The union plans to continue the collective action and launch an indefinite strike next Wednesday unless the management responds to its demands for an additional hiring of 1,313 personnel and a wage increase of 3.5 percent.
It has also called for the management to scrap a plan to cut 2,212 jobs.
Unionized workers of Korea Railroad Corp. (KORAIL) have also warned of launching an indefinite general strike on Dec. 10, demanding the hiring of more safety-related personnel.
